extracted.intended_audience: computer scientists, NLP and ML researchers, and interdisciplinary scholars (psychology, social science, linguistics) working on media-bias detection and analysis
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic literature-review and taxonomy of media-bias types and computational methods for detecting them, summarizing definitions, subtypes, datasets, and methodological best practices. Intended to organize concepts across computer science and social sciences and to guide future automated media-bias research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Bias (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Media bias describes slanted news coverage or other biased media content; it can be intentional (expressing a tendency towards a perspective, ideology, or result) or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this umbrella definition to anchor distinctions among subtypes; the review focuses on text-based media bias and clarifies overlap among concepts used in different disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic Bias (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern of using certain words that reflects a particular way of thinking about a group or an individual; involves systematic preference for certain words or phrases that may reflect stereotypes or preconceived notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes five subtypes (linguistic intergroup bias, framing bias, epistemological bias, bias by semantic properties, connotation bias). Detectable via word choice, lexical resources, and linguistic feature analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic Intergroup Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes which group members use specific language; based on the linguistic category model (LCM), which categorizes words into different abstraction levels (action words, interpretive action words, state verbs, adjectives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for differences in abstraction levels when describing in-group vs out-group (e.g., 'A is punching B' vs 'A is aggressive'). Useful feature for identifying subtle stereotype reinforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing Bias (linguistic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of 'subjective words or phrases linked with a particular point of view' to sway the meaning of a statement; subjective words include one-sided terms and subjective intensifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect via subjectivity clues, lexicons of one-sided terms; examples: choosing 'McMansions' vs neutral term, or using 'pro-life' vs 'anti-abortion' framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistemological Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of linguistic features that subtly focus on the credibility of a statement (word classes like factive verbs, entailments, assertive verbs, hedges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify factive verbs (presuppose truth), entailments (one statement implies another), assertive verbs (imply affirmative opinion), and hedges (introduce vagueness). These features subtly influence perceived truthfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias by Semantic Properties
rubrics_metrics.description: How word choice and sentence structure affect framing and trigger bias; refers to grammatical/semantic alternations (e.g., causative–inchoative alternations) that emphasize different interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze syntax–semantics interface; examples include 'Rebecca broke the pencil' vs 'The pencil broke' which foreground actor vs event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connotation Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Using connotations (secondary, emotional meanings) to introduce bias even when denotations are identical (e.g., 'immigrants' vs 'aliens', 'estate tax' vs 'death tax').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect via paired term lists and embedding distances; connotative polarity (positive/negative) is a key signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factive Verbs (feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbs that presuppose the truth of a complement clause (e.g., 'realized' implies truth of complement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count/use as features indicating epistemological bias; treat as stronger indicators of presented certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entailments (feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directional relations where one statement implies the truth of another (used to signal or imply facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model entailment relations to surface implicit assertions or presuppositions that bias interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertive Verbs (feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbs that imply an affirmative opinion on the truth value of a complement (e.g., 'regret', 'resent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as indicators of presented stance/certainty; helpful for epistemological-bias detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hedge Words (feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words used to lessen probability and the writer’s guarantee of truthfulness (e.g., 'perhaps', 'might', 'may').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of hedges signals uncertainty framing; incorporate in models to detect subtle distancing or epistemic modulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-level Context Bias (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias that arises from how the context within a text is expressed; words and statements alter article context influencing readers' opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes statement bias, phrasing bias, and spin bias (omission and informational). Consider inter-dependencies between words and phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the media interjecting their own opinions into the text, producing reporting that is more or less favorable toward a position; may be faint and expressed by disproportionate criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect subjective insertions, evaluative language, or asymmetric criticism; examine presence of opinionated clauses within ostensibly factual passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrasing Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterized by inflammatory or non-neutral language; words can be neutral in some contexts and inflammatory in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual analysis required; employ phrase-level polarity and contextual sentiment to flag phrasing bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin Bias (text level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias introduced by omitting necessary information (omission/simplification) or adding unnecessary/speculative/tangential information (informational/exaggeration) to craft a memorable story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate omission vs added speculation; examine coverage of facts vs speculative framing for the same event across sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission Bias / Simplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving out necessary information from a story (simplification) to shape narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare versions of stories across outlets; look for missing factual elements that change interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational Bias / Exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding speculative, tangential, or irrelevant information to a news story to influence interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect speculative language, counterfactuals, or tangential claims that are not supported by core evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting-level Context Bias (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias at the level of what topics/events receive attention and how they are covered across outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes selection/gatekeeping bias, coverage bias, and proximity bias; operationalize via counts, space/placement, and article length measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Bias / Gatekeeping Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of content to report by writers and editors; not all events are reported and editorial choices are prone to personal preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure presence/absence of topics across outlets; use editorial-choices analysis and heuristics for missing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Imbalanced amounts of attention to different sides of an issue (e.g., absolute number of articles, prominence like front-page placement, article length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify via counts, placement, and length; compare across outlets and over time to detect imbalance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to report more about culturally similar or geographically proximate events, leading to imbalanced reporting depth and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include geographic and cultural similarity features when modeling coverage disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Bias (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias arising from how readers process media information (systematic deviations from rationality in judgment or decision-making).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes selective exposure, partisan bias, hostile media phenomenon, and other perceptual moderators; important for user-centered evaluation of bias detection systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers actively select which articles they read and tend to favor information consistent with their views, exacerbating bias via echo chambers or filter bubbles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider audience consumption patterns when evaluating impact of bias detection; model selective exposure and its amplification effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisan Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of veracity and perceived bias depends on readers' political identity; people perceive media as biased in line with party affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for partisan identity in perception studies and dataset annotation; measuring perceived bias requires controlling for reader ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile Media Phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of opposing groups tend to rate the same news article as biased against their point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-group annotation and perception measures; account for asymmetric perceptions when validating detection systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal Factors (in perception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors like ideological similarity with peers influence perception of media bias; conversations with like-minded others increase bias perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate social-network and interpersonal-context variables when studying perceived bias and the social amplification of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Comments Influence (on perceived bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposure to other users' comments can alter a reader's perception of bias in an article (comments aligned with a reader’s opinion reduce perceived bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing perceived bias, control for commenting context; comments can be confounds in annotation tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure to Opposing Views (effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant exposure to opposing views may increase perceived bias or shift opinions; e.g., following accounts that retweet opposing content changed views in experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider exposure history of users in evaluation and dataset collection; incorporate temporal exposure controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Identification / Involvedness
rubrics_metrics.description: High involvement or identification with a topic increases likelihood of perceiving media as biased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure participant involvedness during perception studies; adjust annotation protocols for topic salience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet Reputation (effect on perceived bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation or known ideological orientation of an outlet influences perceived bias for the same article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate content-based bias signals from brand/label effects when evaluating detection systems; blind or anonymized evaluation can control for this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Concepts (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts related to or overlapping with media bias but not exclusive to one category: framing effects, hate speech, sentiment analysis, group bias (gender, racial, religion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about inclusion/exclusion (the review excludes fake-news literature); use subfield-specific methods and datasets for each related concept and note overlap with bias types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: How discourse is structured into interpretive packages (frames) that give meaning to an issue, promoting specific interpretations and highlighting some aspects while overlooking others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame analysis methods from social sciences apply; treat frames as higher-level constructs that may aggregate multiple bias signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hate Speech (as related concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language expressing hatred towards a targeted group or intended to derogate; often biased and reinforcing tensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish hate-speech detection from bias-detection tasks but note overlap; hate-speech features can be part of bias-detection pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment Analysis (as tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining text for emotional content or polarity; can detect biases in statements or articles and help identify hate speech or ideological slant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentiment as a complementary signal; combine with other linguistic/contextual features for bias detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Bias (umbrella: gender, racial, religion biases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic disproportionate representation or stereotyping of social groups; includes gender bias (under-representation, stereotyped quoting), racial and religion bias (disproportionate representation of minorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize via representation metrics, quoting frequency, embedding associations; watch for manifestation in training data and embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Bias (example of group bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dominance of one gender over others in medium leading to under-representation and stereotypes (e.g., topic- and quote-distributions differing by gender).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure topic-conditional quoting rates, build gender-aware lexicons, and include gender-balance checks in dataset construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Bias and Religion Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic disproportionate representation or negative associations of ethnic or religious groups, sometimes reflected in embeddings (e.g., 'Muslim' near 'terrorist').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as important subdomains; check embedding-space biases and dataset composition; link to hate-speech and group-bias measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional Natural Language Processing (tNLP) methods (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-ML or non-graph-based techniques used to identify media bias, including count-based (word/n-gram counts + lexicons) and embedding-based approaches; often used as baselines due to explainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tNLP is a common baseline and accessible for social science; split into count-based (lexicon/feature engineering) and embedding-based (representations for comparison/association analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Count-Based Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify words and n-grams to analyze bias using lexicons and frequency statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for interpretable baselines; combine with lexical resources; suitable for explainable analyses and social-science use-cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding-Based tNLP Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vector-space representations to compare texts or analyze associations and inherent biases in data (e.g., word embeddings to reveal stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for measuring semantic associations and for downstream bias-detection features; be mindful of biases encoded in embeddings themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformer-based Machine Learning (tbML)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern approaches leveraging transformer architectures (e.g., BERT) for classification and fine-grained bias detection; increasing majority of recent publications use tbML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High performance for fine-grained tasks; evaluate with diverse datasets and perception-related variables; be cautious about domain shifts and explainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Transformer-based ML (ntbML)
rubrics_metrics.description: ML approaches that use architectures other than transformers (e.g., older neural nets or other classifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less prevalent in recent literature; consider as comparative baselines or for constrained-resource settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Neural Network (nNN)-based approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical ML methods (e.g., SVM, logistic regression) or other non-neural algorithms used for bias detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for interpretability, baseline comparisons, and when data are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph-based Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches leveraging graph learning (e.g., social networks, citation/link graphs) to uncover media-bias signals via relational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to incorporate network/infrastructure and audience homophily features; combine with textual signals for improved detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Classification Principle (for reviewing papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify computer-science contributions primarily by the methods they employ (tNLP, tbML, ntbML, nNN, graph-based). If a paper covers multiple categories, assign the most used category; if two apply equally, assign based on best-performing method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use method category as main organizing axis when surveying literature; report counts per year/category and note trends (tbML increasing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic Review Retrieval & Selection Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated, keyword-based retrieval from DBLP and Semantic Scholar (and Google Scholar for non-CS literature), merging and deduplication, followed by multi-stage manual filtering by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeframe Jan 2019–May 2022; reviewers filtered by title/abstract/text, exported methods/datasets per paper; selection required at least two of three reviewers to deem a paper suitable; excluded references of selected papers as additional candidates; detailed selection criteria and code made public in repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset & Evaluation Recommendation (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting media bias requires diverse and reliable bias assessment strategies and datasets that incorporate user and perception-related variables to improve accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate psychological and social-science variables into dataset annotation and evaluation; be explicit about annotation protocols, annotator characteristics, and cross-disciplinary measures when benchmarking models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation/Reviewer Agreement Protocol (for inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each candidate publication in selection, initial reviewer inspects and exports methods/datasets; second reviewer verifies; third consulted if disagreement; at least two reviewers must agree for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-reviewer verification to mitigate selection bias; document disagreements and resolution process; make selection criteria public for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/Timeframe Criterion for Review Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit literature to publications within chosen timeframe (here Jan 2019–May 2022) to provide state-of-the-art overview while keeping search tractable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about timeframe in systematic reviews; note that the review does not cover all years and that trends beyond the timeframe may continue.
